questions.questionText: She ____ in Coimbatore since 2019.
questions.explanation: Since + a point in time, for a state that began in the past and continues now, takes the present perfect: has lived.

questions.questionText: The train ____ before we reached the platform.
questions.explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier one uses the past perfect. Leaving happened before reaching, so: had left.

questions.questionText: Water ____ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts and universal truths use the simple present: boils.

questions.questionText: I ____ my homework when the lights went out.
questions.explanation: A longer ongoing past action interrupted by a shorter one (went out, simple past) takes the past continuous: was doing.

questions.questionText: By next June, Ravi ____ his degree.
questions.explanation: 'By + a future time' signals an action finished before that time: future perfect, will have completed.

questions.questionText: Look! The children ____ in the rain.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' points to an action happening right now: present continuous, are playing.

questions.questionText: He ____ to Madurai last Sunday.
questions.explanation: A finished time marker (last Sunday) requires the simple past: went.

questions.questionText: My father ____ the newspaper every morning.
questions.explanation: 'Every morning' shows a habit: simple present, reads.

questions.questionText: They ____ their lunch yet.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' in a negative sentence goes with the present perfect: have not finished. (Also 'did not finished' is wrong: after did not, the verb stays in base form.)

questions.questionText: Neha ____ sushi in her life.
questions.explanation: 'In her life' covers time up to now, so the present perfect is used: has never eaten.

questions.questionText: No sooner had he entered the room than the phone ____.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had + V3 ... than' is followed by the simple past: rang.
questions.shortcut: No sooner had ... than + simple past.

questions.questionText: Hardly had the match begun when it ____ to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had + V3 ... when' is followed by the simple past: started.

questions.questionText: I ____ for two hours before the manager called me in for the interview.
questions.explanation: A continuous action lasting up to a past moment ('before the manager called') takes the past perfect continuous: had been waiting.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: I have known him since childhood.
I am knowing him since childhood.
I was knowing him since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not used in continuous tenses. Since + point in time needs the present perfect: have known.

questions.questionText: By the time we reached the cinema, the film ____.
questions.explanation: The film started before we arrived (a past moment), so the earlier action uses the past perfect.

questions.questionText: I will call you as soon as I ____ home.
questions.explanation: In time clauses (as soon as, when, after, before, until) the future is expressed by the simple present, not will: reach.

questions.questionText: Ravi ____ in Chennai for ten years before he moved to Pune.
questions.explanation: 'Before he moved' fixes a past reference point; a state lasting up to it takes the past perfect: had lived.

questions.questionText: Tomorrow at this time, we ____ in the exam hall.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future moment takes the future continuous: will be sitting.

questions.questionText: The manager ____ the report since morning but has not finished it.
questions.explanation: 'Since morning' plus an action still unfinished takes the present perfect continuous: has been preparing.

questions.questionText: While the teacher ____ the lesson, two students were chatting.
questions.explanation: Two simultaneous past actions in progress take the past continuous in both clauses: was explaining / were chatting.

questions.questionText: I ____ you last week, but you were out.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' is a finished time, so the simple past is required: called.

questions.questionText: The earthquake occurred while the villagers ____.
questions.explanation: 'While' with a past action in progress takes the past continuous: were sleeping.

questions.questionText: I will phone you after the meeting ____.
questions.explanation: In an 'after' time clause the future is shown by the simple present: ends.

questions.questionText: It is high time you ____ preparing for the exam.
questions.explanation: 'It is (high) time + subject' is followed by the simple past (unreal present urgency): started.

questions.questionText: Ravi is not at home; he ____ to the market.
questions.explanation: 'Has gone' means he is still there; 'has been' means he went and came back. He is not at home, so: has gone.

questions.questionText: My cousin ____ in Dubai for five years now.
questions.explanation: 'For five years now' shows an activity continuing up to the present: present perfect continuous, has been working.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correct?
options: I have been seeing him yesterday.
questions.explanation: A definite finished time (yesterday) cannot be used with the present perfect; use the simple past: saw.

questions.questionText: By the time you read this letter, I ____ for Mumbai.
questions.explanation: 'By the time' + a future moment shows completion before it: future perfect, will have left.

questions.questionText: This is the first time I ____ a motorbike.
questions.explanation: 'This is the first time' takes the present perfect: have ridden.
questions.shortcut: This is the first time + present perfect.

questions.questionText: He ____ the exam three times before he finally passed it.
questions.explanation: The failures happened before the later past event (passed), so the past perfect is used: had failed.

questions.questionText: By next April, Mrs Iyer ____ in this school for twenty years.
questions.explanation: 'By + future time' with duration ('for twenty years') takes the future perfect continuous: will have been teaching.

questions.questionText: Since the project began, the team ____ three major problems.
questions.explanation: 'Since + past event' with an unfinished period up to now takes the present perfect: has faced.

questions.questionText: She ____ the piano for years, so she plays very well.
questions.explanation: A long activity continuing up to now, with 'for years', takes the present perfect continuous: has been playing.
